items.title: Decoding the CLOSURE-AF trial: new insights and a call for critical review.
items.abstract: Graphical AbstractA critical review of the CLOSURE-AF trial and lessons learned. Concerns about patient selection (bias), procedural safety and post-procedural medical therapy are raised. The CLOSURE-AF trial mainly enrolled high-risk, multi-morbid patients, for whom LAAC did not yield net clinical benefit compared with OAC therapy. LAAC, left atrial appendage closure; OAC, oral anticoagulant.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

items.title: Baseline right ventricular assessment and outcomes after transcatheter tricuspid valve repair.
items.abstract: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) and right ventricular (RV) remodelling are closely related. Recent European Society of Cardiology/European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery guidelines on valvular heart disease propose adjusted reference values for RV size and function. To determine the predictive value of the proposed RV dilatation and dysfunction thresholds in a real-world interventional cohort. Echocardiographic thresholds were evaluated retrospectively in 651 patients, who underwent transcatheter tricuspid valve repair (TTVr) at two tertiary centres.The primary endpoint was 2-year survival [Kaplan-Meier estimate: 78.6% (74.9-81.9)]. RV strain was the most frequent marker of dysfunction at baseline [free walls strain (FWS) 24 mm/m 2 ), mid (>21 mm/m 2 ), and tricuspid annular (TA) diameters (>21 mm/m 2 ) were associated with survival ( P = .04, P = .24), whereas tissue doppler imaging s' P = .04; .01). Severe RV dysfunction (FWS P 21 mm/m 2 [hazard ratio (HR) 2.85 (1.41-5.76); P P = .03] independently predicted survival. Mortality risk increased for each additional pathological parameter [HR per parameter 1.33 (1.14-1.57); P n = 341, 52%), no RV cut-off remained associated with survival. TTVr is often performed at an advanced disease stage, and adverse RV remodelling is strongly associated with survival. Nevertheless, effective TR reduction attenuated this prognostic value.

items.title: Latest-iteration self-expanding vs balloon-expandable transcatheter heart valves for failed surgical bioprostheses: The INNOVATE registry.
items.abstract: Valve-in-valve (ViV) transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly performed in degenerated surgical bioprostheses, although data concerning the performance of latest iterations of transcatheter heart valves (THVs) are scarce. We aimed to compare procedural, clinical and haemodynamic outcomes of latest-generation THVs in ViV TAVI. This multicenter retrospective study included 381 consecutive patients undergoing ViV TAVI, 294 with self-expanding (SE), and 87 with a balloon expandable (BE) THV. Primary efficacy endpoints were Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3 technical and device success. Primary safety outcomes were all-cause death and re-hospitalization for heart failure (HF). Patients receiving SE valves were older (79 vs 75 years, P P = .041). A numerically higher rate of coronary obstruction (4% vs 0%, P = .076) was observed in SE THVs, despite a more frequent coronary protection (24% vs 14%, P = .045). Technical (95% vs 98%, P = .380) and device success (89% vs 79%, P = .105) were similar. At 1 year, SE valves showed significantly lower mean gradients (14 ± 8 vs 21 ± 8 mmHg, P P = .928) and re-hospitalization for HF (4% vs 2%, P = .507) was also comparable among SE and BE, likewise myocardial infarction, stroke, and permanent pacemaker implantation. Latest iterations of SE and BE THVs provided favourable outcomes in ViV TAVI, without significant differences in safety/efficacy profile. SE platforms achieved lower residual gradients at 1 year.

items.title: Late outcomes of early discharge following transcatheter aortic valve implantation: results from the POLESTAR trial.
items.abstract: Early discharge (ED) within 48 h after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) seems feasible and safe. The POLESTAR study demonstrated good 30-day outcomes of ED after TAVI using the ACURATE valve but also identified patients requiring prolonged hospitalization. Long-term outcomes after ED or prolonged hospitalization remain unknown. To determine the long-term impact of successful ED and prolonged hospitalization. POLESTAR was a prospective, multicentre, observational trial enrolling patients deemed eligible for ED prior to transfemoral TAVI with ACURATE Neo/Neo2. One-year outcomes were determined and compared between those who achieved ED and those who did not. The primary endpoint was a landmark analysis of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including all-cause mortality, stroke, myocardial infarction, and cardiac rehospitalization, occurring between 30 days and oneyear post-procedure. Among 252 patients from 15 sites in four countries, ED was achieved in 173 (69%) patients, while 79 (31%) required prolonged hospital stay (non-ED). One-year survival was 97%. Landmark 30-day analysis showed MACE occurring in 4.7% of ED patients vs 11.7% of non-ED patients at 1 year (HR 0.38[0.15-0.98] P = .045). Rehospitalization was numerically lower in the ED group (HR 0.56[0.27-1.19]; P = .13). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) scores improved significantly in the full cohort (18.5 improvement; 95%CI: 15.9-21.0, P P for interaction = .30). An ED strategy after TAVI with ACURATE Neo was safe in selected patients without compromising longer-term outcomes or health-related quality of life. Patients who did not achieve ED experienced more MACE after 30 days (NCT03910751).

items.title: eQt Protein Nanocage-Delivered IL-21 mRNA Systemically Reprograms Host Immune Cells Toward Stemness and Maturation to Achieve Anti-Tumor Immunity.
items.abstract: Effective cancer immunotherapy requires reprogramming host immunity toward stem-like states. However, clinical use of IL-21 is limited by short half-life and toxicity. Here, we develop a bio-inspired protein nanocage platform (eQt) that encapsulates IL-21 mRNA via high-affinity λN-boxB interactions during bacterial biosynthesis, enabling one-step manufacturing and pH-responsive endosomal release. eQt-IL-21 drives dendritic cell maturation, characterized by marked upregulation of CD80 and CD86, and transcriptome-wide enrichment of MHC-I antigen processing and presentation pathways (H2-K1, H2-D1, B2m, Tap2), establishing a highly stimulatory environment for T cell priming. Transcriptomic profiling of draining lymph nodes reveals that eQt-IL-21 preferentially diverts CD8 + T-cell differentiation away from terminal exhaustion toward a TCF-1 + /CCR7 + stem-like progenitor identity, with concordant upregulation of Tcf7, Sell (encoding CD62L), and LEF-1, sustaining a self-renewing memory reservoir and long-lived central memory T cells (Tcm). In preclinical E.G7-OVA models, this immunological reprogramming translates into potent prophylactic efficacy and durable therapeutic remission of established tumors, without detectable systemic toxicity. This work establishes IL-21 mRNA-mediated immune-cell reprogramming as a mechanistic cornerstone of durable anti-tumor immunity, and positions the eQt nanocage as a versatile, scalable platform for precision cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: ERN EURO-NMD expert opinion on management of new biologic therapies in myasthenia gravis.
items.abstract: Myasthenia Gravis is a potentially life-threatening autoimmune disease of the neuromuscular junction with fluctuating muscle weakness and fatigability. In recent years, the therapeutic landscape has been notably reshaped by the introduction of new therapies. These agents, primarily acting through complement inhibition or neonatal Fc-receptor blockade, have demonstrated significant efficacy and favorable safety profiles in randomized clinical trials and real-world settings. Their advent has refined clinical management, particularly in refractory patients, leading to meaningful improvements in patients' quality of life and future expectations. Meanwhile, in this evolving therapeutic landscape, new challenges and uncertainties in clinical decision-making have been raised, as new therapies are now part of the standard care in Myasthenia Gravis. Differences in regulatory agency approvals and reimbursement policies across Europe result in heterogeneous access to therapies, complicating treatment decisions and limiting shared real-world experiences. Consequently, clinicians face complex dilemmas regarding optimal patient selection, treatment choice, and long-term management strategies. To address these issues, a panel of experts, including adult and pediatric neurologists and patient representatives, within the framework of the European Reference Network for Neuromuscular Diseases convened to develop consensus-based positions. The aim of this work was to identify, explore, and discuss key challenges associated with the use of new therapies and to propose a practical approach to support clinicians in this rapidly evolving field. Given the variability in clinical approach, treatment availability and reimbursement policies across European healthcare systems, this position paper seeks to provide guidance that are adaptable across diverse settings. A literature review was conducted, focusing on pivotal clinical trials and real-world evidence. Eleven key topics were identified and discussed, and for each, consensus statements were developed and refined through a modified Delphi process: patient assessment from both clinician and patient perspectives; the role of autoantibodies and optimization of serological testing; selection of immunotherapies; definitions of treatment response and failure in the context of new therapies; strategies for switching between therapies; predictors of treatment response; management of concomitant therapies, including corticosteroids and conventional immunosuppressant; discontinuation strategies; their potential role as early-line therapies; their applicability in ocular MG; and future therapeutic perspectives, including ongoing clinical trials. In conclusion, new therapies represent a major advance in Myasthenia Gravis care but also introduce significant complexity. This expert position paper provides a framework to support clinicians in decision-making and highlights the need for harmonized guidelines and further research to optimize their use in routine practice.

items.title: Precision medicine in genitourinary malignancies: integrating molecular profiling into clinical practice.
items.abstract: Molecular profiling increasingly guides genitourinary cancer management, but biomarker maturity and clinical utility vary across prostate, urothelial, renal, and testicular cancers. This review examines homologous recombination repair (HRR) and germline testing, PARP inhibition, and PSMA theranostics in prostate cancer; FGFR3-targeted therapy and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-guided adjuvant immunotherapy in urothelial carcinoma; predictive biomarker limitations and HIF-2α-directed therapy in renal cell carcinoma; and investigational serum miR-371a-3p in testicular cancer. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from January 2016 through October 2026, supplemented by conference proceedings and clinical guidelines. Germline testing informs treatment selection and hereditary-risk assessment in prostate cancer, but remains selective in urothelial and renal cancers, primarily for hereditary-risk assessment, with syndrome-directed therapy in von Hippel-Lindau disease. It has no established role in testicular cancer. Molecular profiling currently guides management in prostate and urothelial cancers. In renal cancer, PD-L1 and tumor mutational burden remain non-predictive, while transcriptomic signatures are investigational. In testicular cancer, miR-371a-3p outperforms conventional serum markers diagnostically but cannot detect teratoma, and its clinical utility remains unvalidated.

items.title: Elevated serum KIF20A in hepatocellular carcinoma: exploring its potential as a circulating biomarker.
items.abstract: To evaluate serum KIF20A expression in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and assess its association with HCC status using a bioinformatics-guided clinical RT-qPCR approach. This cross-sectional study included 110 participants: 50 with HCC, 10 with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection without HCC, and 50 healthy controls. Serum hsa-miR-5192, HSPA1B, LPH02229A/CRHR1-IT1, and KIF20A were quantified by RT-qPCR as relative quantification (RQ). Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) was the conventional comparator. Secondary analyses evaluated AFP with KIF20A using logistic regression, AUC comparison, and repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation. KIF20A showed significant overall differential expression (P=0.003), with higher expression in HCC than in healthy controls (P=0.007) and the HCV non-HCC group (P=0.004). Median KIF20A RQ was 2.95 in HCC, 0.40 in healthy controls, and 0.255 in HCV. For HCC versus all non-HCC participants, KIF20A remained associated with HCC after accounting for AFP (OR 2.10 per 1-SD increase in log-transformed KIF20A; 95% CI 1.01-4.37; P=0.048), but the combined model did not materially improve discrimination over AFP alone (AUC 0.968 vs 0.964; DeLong P=0.606). Serum KIF20A showed HCC-associated upregulation and retained an exploratory association with HCC after accounting for AFP. However, it did not provide meaningful incremental discrimination beyond AFP; the small disease-control group and absence of external validation preclude claims of HCC specificity or clinical diagnostic readiness.

items.title: HTLV infection among pregnant women attending a viral hepatitis referral center in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
items.abstract: Human T-cell lymphotropic virus (HTLV) remains a neglected infection worldwide, despite its potential for severe disease and vertical transmission. In Brazil, the burden of HTLV infection among pregnant remains poorly understood, underscoring the need for updated epidemiological data to guide elimination strategies. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence and socio-epidemiological profile of HTLV infection in pregnant receiving care at a referral center in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. We conducted a mixed (retrospective and prospective) cohort study of 403 pregnant (409 gestational events) referred between 2016 and 2024. All participants were screened for HTLV-1/2 using chemiluminescent immunoassay and confirmed by Western blot. Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected from medical records. HTLV testing was performed in 305 pregnant, with four confirmed infections (prevalence of 1.31% [CI 0,36% - 3,32%]). Three cases (75%) were HTLV-1 and one (25%) HTLV-2. Most women self-identified as mixed race (75%) and had low educational attainment (75%). Coinfections with HBV, HCV, and HIV were detected in 50%, 50%, and 25% of cases, respectively. HTLV prevalence among pregnant was higher than some previous regional estimates, underscoring the need for timely diagnosis to mitigate the risk of new infections. These findings underscore the need for universal antenatal screening, health education, and targeted public health interventions to prevent vertical transmission in Brazil.

items.title: Correlation between maternal serum pgRNA levels during pregnancy and neonatal virological characteristics at birth in HBV-infected pregnant women.
items.abstract: To investigate the relationship between serum pregenomic RNA (pgRNA) in pregnant women with chronic HBV (CHB) infection during pregnancy and maternal clinical characteristics, virological characteristics of newborns at birth, and mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) outcomes. 312 pregnant women with CHB and their newborns were followed up for 12 months, and their clinical data were collected. Spearman correlation analysis was used to evaluate associations between maternal indicators and neonatal outcomes, and logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with neonatal HBeAg positivity. Maternal HBV DNA, HBsAg, and HBeAg levels were significantly higher in the pgRNA-positive group. All infants followed up to 12 months were negative for both HBsAg and HBV DNA, yielding a 100% success rate of MTCT prevention. Neonatal HBeAg levels at birth were associated with maternal pgRNA levels. Maternal pgRNA levels were significantly higher in mothers of HBeAg-positive newborns than in those of HBeAg-negative newborns, whereas no significant association was found between maternal pgRNA levels and neonatal HBsAg or HBV DNA status. Neonatal HBeAg level was weakly positively correlated with maternal pgRNA levels (r = 0.17, P < 0.01) and maternal HBeAg levels (r = 0.12, P < 0.05). Maternal pgRNA, HBeAg, HBsAg, HBV DNA, age, and treatment were identified as factors associated with neonatal HBeAg status, whereas multivariate analysis showed that only maternal HBeAg remained an independent associated factor. Maternal serum pgRNA is associated with neonatal HBeAg status at birth. However, under standardized combined immunoprophylaxis, maternal pgRNA was not associated with MTCT failure.

items.title: Candidate epistatic mutation clusters in occult hepatitis B virus genotype D: a critical narrative review of the evidence gap and a proposed testable framework.
items.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) genotype D is the dominant genotype across the Middle East. It forms the background against which diagnostic assays, blood-screening algorithms, and vaccination programmes operate in the region. Occult hepatitis B infection (OBI), the presence of replication-competent HBV DNA in individuals who test negative for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), remains a persistent challenge for diagnosis, for transfusion and transplant safety, and for the management of immunosuppressed patients. Individual surface-protein escape mutations are well characterised, yet they account only incompletely for the full spectrum of OBI. It is not yet established whether combinations of co-occurring surface mutations interact non-additively, that is epistatically, to influence HBsAg detectability, secretion, or replication in genotype D, whether such combinations are enriched in Middle Eastern populations, or whether they are shaped by HIV or HCV coinfection. The functional and structural data required to answer these questions are largely absent. We critically appraise the available evidence, separate established findings from extrapolation and hypothesis using an explicit grading scheme, and propose a testable bioinformatic and experimental framework to determine whether candidate epistatic clusters contribute to OBI in genotype D. We propose and apply a four-level evidence hierarchy distinguishing co-occurrence, phylogenetically corrected covariation, experimental single-versus-combination comparison, and mechanistic validation. Against this hierarchy, published data on HBsAg mutation clusters in genotype D reach Level 1-2 at most; the decisive Level 3 experiment, site-directed reconstruction of candidate clusters versus their constituent single mutants on a defined genotype D backbone, has not been performed. Genotype-D-specific and Middle-East-specific datasets adequate for cluster-level analysis are limited, direct evidence linking coinfection to selection of mutation clusters is absent, and structural inference remains constrained because recent cryo-EM structures of HBsAg subviral particles do not resolve the 'a' determinant loops at the resolution required to interpret mutation-cluster-level conformational perturbations. Epistasis is a biologically plausible, under-tested mechanism that may help explain why single mutations incompletely account for OBI. It should not be presented as an established driver. We define the sequencing, functional, structural, and clinical studies required to test the hypothesis directly, and we identify the methodological safeguards, particularly phylogenetic correction, that any such effort must adopt.

items.title: Comparative analysis of SNPs associated with COVID-19 and chronic liver disease identifies DPP9 as a candidate genetic marker for Long COVID.
items.abstract: Long COVID is a multisystemic condition characterized by persistent symptoms after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, whose biological mechanisms are not yet fully understood. Host genetic factors may be associated, and the sharing of genetic architecture with other chronic diseases such as viral hepatitis B and C may aid in understanding this disease. A cross-sectional study was conducted including 150 individuals stratified into two groups: (i) Long COVID and (ii) chronic viral hepatitis B and C. Eighteen single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) previously associated with COVID-19 severity and inflammatory pathways were genotyped using TaqMan® real-time PCR assays. The analyses of genetic association models were performed using multivariate logistic regression adjusted for gender, self-reported skin color, and comorbidities. Mental health scales for assessing depression (Beck), anxiety (Hamilton), fatigue, and post-COVID functional scale were used both to define the syndrome and for subsequent analyses of the genotypic profile probably associated with Long COVID. Among all the SNPs analyzed, rs12610495 (A/G) in the DPP9 gene was the only variant consistently associated with Long COVID. After adjustment for sex, self-reported skin color, and hepatitis status, carriers of the G variant allele demonstrated increased odds of Long COVID under the dominant model (OR = 2.66; 95% CI: 1.08-6.57; p = 0.029) and the overdominant model (OR = 2.96; 95% CI: 1.17-7.52; p = 0.018). The association was more pronounced in women (OR = 3.30; 95% CI: 1.08-10.07). Exploratory analyses of mental and functional outcomes did not reach statistical significance, although a higher frequency of functional limitation and fatigue was observed among carriers of the G allele. This study suggests that DPP9 rs12610495 is associated with Long COVID, previously associated only with severe acute COVID, demonstrating that individuals carrying the rs12610495 G variant allele had higher odds of developing Long COVID. The inclusion of viral hepatitis as a chronic inflammatory condition for comparison contributed to the identification of shared genetic archetypal among diseases, revealing the possible role of DPP9 with Long COVID and highlighting this gene as a relevant target for future validation studies.

items.title: A multi-scale stress-lactylation blueprint unmasks a macrophage-engineered metabolic trap driving non-canonical CD8⁺ T cell paralysis and dual-targeting vulnerability in hepatocellular carcinoma.
items.abstract: Chronic systemic stress (CSS) is associated with the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet the molecular mechanisms linking physiological exhaustion into intratumoral immune evasion remain fundamentally opaque. We aimed to decode the biological axis bridging systemic allostatic load (AL), lactate metabolism, and localized immune collapse. Leveraging the NHANES cohort, we established epidemiological links between AL, lactate, and mortality. An integrative consensus machine-learning framework derived a stress-lactylation signature (SLS). We mapped the SLS-associated microenvironment via single-cell/spatial transcriptomics, dissecting mechanistic interactions through in silico network perturbations and pharmacogenomics, which were subsequently corroborated by comprehensive ex vivo clinical tissue analyses and in vitro functional co-culture validations. High AL independently predicted elevated all-cause mortality in adults with liver dysfunction, correlating robustly with systemic lactate. Projecting this macro-level vulnerability into the tumor microenvironment, we distilled a 6-gene SLS as a potent HCC prognosticator. Multi-omics deconvolution revealed that high-SLS tumors compartmentalize into immunosuppressive niches where SPP1⁺ macrophages mediate the metabolic suppression of CD8⁺ T cells. Crucially, ex vivo analyses of HCC patient tissues verified elevated histone lactylation (H3K9la) and its profound spatial co-localization with active glycolysis (GLUT1⁺) and SPP1⁺ macrophages. Furthermore, in vitro co-culture models confirmed that blocking tumor-derived lactate directly attenuates M2-like polarization and downregulates SPP1 expression in recipient macrophages. Finally, Adavosertib was functionally validated as a precision dual-targeting agent, effectively inhibiting both upstream tumor lactate production and downstream macrophage-associated remodeling (CTSS). We delineate a comprehensive multi-scale blueprint linking CSS to localized immune failure. The SLS provides an accurate prognostic tool, while our experimental validations expose a lactate-driven macrophage metabolic trap, unveiling a precision dual-inhibition strategy to reinvigorate anti-tumor immunity in stress-burdened HCC.

items.title: Di/tripeptides in cancer: from mechanisms to therapeutics.
items.abstract: Research on tumor metabolic reprogramming has long centered on glucose, lipids and free amino acids. By contrast, di/tripeptides, which lie at the interface between protein breakdown products and functional metabolic signals, have only recently begun to be recognized as a distinct molecular tier in cancer biology. Compared with longer peptides, di/tripeptides display greater metabolic mobility and a clearer dependence on dedicated transport systems. Here we systematically review the sources, transport, metabolic use, biological functions and clinical translational potential of di/tripeptides in cancer. Current evidence indicates that di/tripeptides arise from endogenous protein degradation, dietary digestion and microbial metabolism. Under nutrient limitation, tumor cells can recover amino acids through carnosine dipeptidase 2 (CNDP2)-mediated extracellular cleavage of dipeptides or uptake of intact di/tripeptides followed by intracellular hydrolysis. Beyond their role as nutrient substrates, selected di/tripeptides directly influence tumor cell proliferation, invasion, metastasis and drug resistance, and shape the tumor microenvironment by modulating acid base balance, redox homeostasis, angiogenesis and immune cell function. At the clinical translational level, di/tripeptides have emerged as candidate metabolomic and peptidomic biomarkers, transporter targeted imaging probes, functionally modified therapeutic agents and engineered delivery modules. Di/tripeptides should be viewed as molecular nodes that connect tumor nutrient adaptation, signaling control, microenvironmental remodeling and clinical translation, with significance extending beyond their role as transient intermediates in protein metabolism.

items.title: Associations of CLivD score with dementia, cardiovascular disease, cancer, and mortality in the general population from the UK biobank.
items.abstract: The Chronic Liver Disease (CLivD) score is a non-invasive marker of advanced liver disease risk. We evaluated its associations with dementia, cardiovascular disease (CVD), cancer, and all-cause mortality. This prospective cohort study included UK Biobank participants with calculable CLivD scores at baseline (2006-2010). Two previously validated versions of the score were calculated: a laboratory-based CLivD (CLivD lab ), incorporating age, sex, waist-hip ratio, alcohol consumption, diabetes, smoking, and gamma-glutamyltransferase (GGT), and a non-laboratory CLivD (CLivD nonlab ), based on the same predictors without GGT. Data were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models, Kaplan-Meier survival curves, and restricted cubic spline functions. Additional models adjusted for centered age and sex. This prospective cohort study included 88,449 UK Biobank participants with calculable CLivD scores (2006-2010) and a mean 9.76-year follow-up. During follow-up, 1,052 (1.19%) developed dementia, 8,814 (9.97%) experienced CVD, 15,882 (17.96%) were diagnosed with cancer, and 4,944 (5.59%) participants died. Compared to the lowest CLivD quartile (Q1), the highest quartile (Q4) was associated with significantly elevated risks of dementia (CLivD lab : HR = 5.57, 95% CI [4.37-7.11]; CLivD nonlab : HR = 4.39, 95% CI [3.51-5.50] ), CVD (CLivD lab : HR = 4.23, 95% CI [3.93-4.55]; CLivD nonlab : HR = 3.59, 95% CI [3.34-3.85] ), cancer (CLivD lab : HR = 2.27, 95% CI [2.17-2.38]; CLivD nonlab : HR = 2.11, 95% CI [2.01-2.21] ), and mortality (CLivD lab : HR = 4.77, 95% CI [4.31-5.28]; CLivD nonlab : HR = 4.14, 95% CI [3.76-4.56] ), all p values  lab quartile remained associated with all four outcomes. Higher CLivD scores were also associated with Alzheimer's disease, vascular dementia, stroke, coronary heart disease, and heart failure. Kaplan-Meier curves showed higher cumulative incidence across increasing CLivD quartiles, and most dose-response associations were nonlinear. Higher CLivD scores identified individuals at increased risk of dementia, cardiovascular disease, cancer, and all-cause mortality in the general population. These findings support CLivD as a broad risk stratification marker, while its interpretation should account for demographic components embedded in the score and requires validation in more diverse populations.

items.title: CalliSpheres ® drug-eluting beads transarterial chemoembolization versus conventional transarterial chemoembolization in patients with refractory liver metastases: a propensity score-matched multi-center study.
items.abstract: CalliSpheres ® is the first domestically developed drug-eluting bead product in China. Although its therapeutic efficacy has been reported in primary liver cancer, clinical data remain limited for patients with refractory liver metastases failing standard systemic therapy, and head-to-head comparisons between CalliSpheres ® drug-eluting beads transarterial chemoembolization (DEB-TACE) and conventional TACE (cTACE) are scarce. This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of the two interventional modalities for refractory liver metastases. This retrospective multi-center study enrolled patients with refractory liver metastases who received DEB-TACE or cTACE across four clinical centers between January 2018 and December 2021. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to balance confounding bias. Tumor response was assessed at 1, 3 and 6 months post-procedure per RECIST version 1.1 criteria. Primary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS); secondary endpoints consisted of disease control rate (DCR), quality of life (assessed via QLQ-C30), liver function parameters and adverse events. A total of 102 patients received DEB-TACE and 118 received cTACE. After PSM, 58 patients remained in each group with balanced baseline characteristics. The DEB-TACE group had significantly higher ORR at 1, 3 and 6 months than the cTACE group (58.6% vs. 34.5%, P = 0.001; 48.3% vs. 27.6%, P = 0.009; 44.8% vs. 25.9%, P = 0.038). Median PFS (10.5 vs. 6.7 months, P = 0.003) and median OS (25.2 vs. 15.7 months, P = 0.006) were significantly prolonged in the DEB-TACE group. Multivariate Cox regression analysis demonstrated that cTACE was an independent adverse risk factor for PFS (HR = 1.72, P = 0.009) and OS (HR = 1.65, P = 0.026). The degrees of postoperative day-4 elevations in ALT and AST as well as the incidence of abdominal pain were significantly lower in the DEB-TACE group (all P < 0.05). There were no grade ≥ 3 serious adverse events in either group. CalliSpheres ® DEB-TACE achieves superior ORR, PFS and OS and better safety compared with cTACE for patients with refractory liver metastases. Prospective randomized controlled trials are warranted to validate these findings.
